pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
TEDDY'S LITTLE BIGGEST ADVENTURE

The littlest dog. The biggest day.

It is Teddy's birthday. Nobody says so.

Doc Leo says "Good morning, buddy!" and hands Teddy a list of errands. Gwinn's bed is empty (again). Teddy doesn't say anything. He is a professional. But his ears droop a little, and so does his grin. Just a little.

So off they go in THE CHEZ, Doc Leo's little red CitiCar: the garage, Maple Street, Puddlewick Park, Downtown, the river and the old mill, the Fair's funhouse, a firefly meadow, and up Lookout Hill to the Clown Club's Big Top. At each of Teddy's stops there is something on the list to fetch for Doc Leo. He says it is just errands.

It is not just errands. Every so often the story says MEANWHILE... and you see what everybody else is up to: you play Gwinn, delivering invitations and digging up her best bone, or Doc Leo, twisting balloon dogs, ducking practice pies and hanging the party lights. Teddy won't see any of it. Please don't tell him.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type TEDDY3 and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster (or compatible) plays the music and the digitized woofs, boofs, honks and squawks; without one, the PC speaker does its best.

A cartoon plays first (pick Read Storyline to see it again). Press any key for the menu, then pick Play. Leave the menu alone for half a minute and Teddy will show you round the garage himself.

There are seventeen stops, one of them a dream. Before each one a card shows which stop it is (LEVEL 2 OF 17), where you are, what to look for, and what is new. Who you play changes from stop to stop: Teddy, Gwinn, Doc Leo, or THE CHEZ on the road.

Energy and naps

The whole team shares one energy (the F2 screen calls it Hitpoints) and three naps (Lives). Pests, pies and potholes wear you down; bones give 25 back, balloon dogs 10. Bones get scarce after the old mill, and the back half's pies, sandbags and spotlights sting harder, so mind your energy. When it runs out it's nap time, and you start the stop over. When the naps are all used up, the game is over.

Press F5 to save your game and F6 to load it.

pages.head: Teddy
pages.html:
Teddy

A red-gold corgi with a white blaze and a ton of tricks (he knows left from right, which is more than most dogs can say).

Left Right (A D)Walk.
Up (W)Hop. Hold it to hop higher, let go to steer. Q and E hop up and left or right in one go.
SpaceWOOF. Mice, pigeons and squirrels clear out.
DownDig. Soft dirt, buried bones.
FFetch what you're standing on.
SSniff by a faint wisp: whatever hides there turns up (sleepy fireflies wake up).
1High five: and new, buttons. A spark runs down the button's wire to what it opens. Some doors close again by themselves: push, then run.
2Sit pretty for anybody asking SIT?
3Spin: turnstiles.
4Play dead (hold): pies and discs fly over.

At the end of each of Teddy's stops, Doc Leo waits by THE CHEZ, his thought bubble showing what's on the list. Bring it and the car door opens.

pages.head: Gwinn and Doc Leo
pages.html:
Gwinn and Doc Leo

Gwinn (MEANWHILE...)

SpaceBOOF: a big bark that rolls a long way, and rings doorbells.
DownDig big: through hard clay Teddy couldn't scratch.
1Chew: ropes and roots.
2Sit. She is still learning.
3Zoomies!
4Flop (hold): the stage lights go right over her.

Doc Leo (MEANWHILE...)

The friendliest hobo clown in the Clown Club, and two blocks tall. He strolls, hops (Up, Q, E) and fetches (F).

SpaceSQUAWK: he squeezes his rubber chicken, and pigeons can't stand it.
1Balloon dog: he twists one, it inflates right under his shoes and floats him up six blocks, then bobs a moment and pops. Step off before it does. Juggling pins pop balloons too.
4Pratfall (hold): flat on his back, so pies and sandbags at head height go over.

pages.head: Driving THE CHEZ
pages.html:
Driving THE CHEZ

On the road trips you drive Doc Leo's tomato-red 1976½ CitiCar, with Teddy riding along.

Left RightDrive (a little quicker than Teddy trots).
UpBump on the springs: over a speed bump, out of a pothole. Q and E bump along.
SpaceHONK! Geese and ducks flap off the road, and a bridge keeper lowers the drawbridge. (A cow does not care. Wait for her.)

Charge

THE CHEZ is 100% electric. Every hill takes one charge to climb: its foot has a striped barrier with a lightning bolt, and with no charge the barrier stays down. Stop at a charger post by the road and wait: each time its light pulses, that's one charge. Two bolts on a sign means a two-charge climb. There is always a charger somewhere on the road.

pages.head: Things to Find
pages.html:
Things to Find

Treats and bones

Dog biscuits everywhere, 10 points each (the F2 screen counts them as Money). A bone gives back 25 energy.

Balloon dogs

Doc Leo's pink balloon animals bob somewhere in most stops: 250 points and 10 energy. (His blue ones are for riding.)

The errands

Doc Leo's garageTHE CHEZ's keys
Puddlewick Parkthe kite's streamers
Downtowna box of birthday candles
The old millthe Clown Club's banner
The funhouseparty horns
Firefly Meadowa paper lantern

(Teddy has not put two and two together. He is a dog.)

RSVPs and the rest

Gwinn collects three RSVP cards for the party van's door. Doc Leo fetches the balloons, the cake and the plug for the lights.

pages.head: Who's Who
pages.html:
Who's Who

  • Teddy: the birthday boy (he is pretty sure).
  • Gwinn: his big sister, keeping a secret for almost a whole day.
  • Doc Leo: the friendliest hobo clown in the Clown Club. Felt fedora, wire glasses, white paint round his eyes and mouth, a sunburned nose, painted stubble, and Reggie the rubber chicken on a leash.
  • THE CHEZ: his little red CitiCar. It charges at about a mile an hour, so it stops at every charger it sees.
  • The Clown Club: Juggles, Honker, Bubbles, Twirly and Professor Pratfall, all practicing for the party.
  • The Town Crier, the baker, the miller and the bridge keeper: friends along the way.

Pests and nuisances

  • Mice, pigeons, squirrels, dust bunnies: woof, boof or squawk.
  • Geese: honk (or boof).
  • Moles: boof.
  • Jack-in-the-boxes: woof and they latch shut.
  • Practice pies, flying discs, sandbags: play dead, flop or pratfall.
  • Cows: wait.

pages.head: The Stops
pages.html:
The Stops

1. Doc Leo's Garage

Bark the mouse out of the laundry room and high-five the button by the door. In the garage, hop onto the workbench and high-five the button over it: the key cabinet opens. Fetch the keys. The garage door's button sends it up for three seconds only: push, then run. Doc Leo's sign by the door folds away only for a dog carrying the keys.

2. Maple Street (THE CHEZ)

You start plugged in. Honk the geese, bump over the speed bump and out of the pothole, and spend your charge on the first hill. The big hill takes two, and its charger is down on the low road, a step below the street: drive down, wait for two pulses, and bump back up. Over the top, more geese and one more pothole.

3. Puddlewick Park

The see-saws: wait on the little red step beside an end and walk on when it comes down level, then ride it up. Over the hedge, across the duck pond end to end, and up Juggles' super see-saw into the oak for the kite's streamers. Play dead under the flying discs.

4. MEANWHILE: Gwinn's Invitations

BOOF a friend's doorbell and they come to the door with an RSVP. The Town Crier, then Honker past the pigeons, then Professor Pratfall up the fire escape behind the alley fence (dig under it). The party van's door takes all three.

5. Downtown

The bakery's conveyor belts. A slow one carries you; walk against the others and hop the gaps. The fast belt flings you across a gap no dog could hop: press E at its very end. The baker has the candles.

6. MEANWHILE: Doc Leo's Balloons

Squawk the pigeons off the hall floor, then twist a balloon dog (1) to float up onto the shelves, shelf to shelf. Juggles' practice pins pop balloons: go up after one flies by. The bag of balloons is in the loft.

7. The River Road (THE CHEZ)

Honk the drawbridge down. Drive onto the ferry at the dock and off the far side with a bump. The last bridge only stays down a few seconds, and there's a two-charge hill right after it: charge first, then honk.

8. The Old Mill

A paddle coming up the near side of a water wheel is a lift. Ride up floor to floor (step on when a paddle is level), then out of the loft down the flume into the millrace, which carries you to the big wheel turning the other way.

pages.head: More Stops
pages.html:
More Stops

9. MEANWHILE: Gwinn's Buried Treasure

Dig down through the layers: soft dirt (one big dig), hard clay (two), rock (go round), roots (chew), moles (boof). Her best bone is at the bottom. The old well's bucket takes her back up.

10. MEANWHILE: Pie Practice

The Clown Club is practicing pie throws. A high wind-up means a pie at head height: pratfall. A low one skids along the floor: hop it. Under the stage, pratfall under a volley, then balloon up in the lull. The cake is at Professor Pratfall's stall.

11. The Funhouse

Red and blue boards blink on a beat over the ball pit: each flashes twice before it goes. Red, then blue. Ride the spinning barrel as the boards come back, then hop up the blinking stairs to the prize stand.

12. Teddy's Dream Run

A bonus: Teddy naps in THE CHEZ and dreams he is running. He hops on the spot while the world runs by. Hop the balls and puddles (hold Up for a higher hop), play dead (4) under the low branches, and hop for the treats. When every paw print in the sky has filled in, the path carries him to the finish.

13. Lookout Hill (THE CHEZ)

Every driving trick at once, all the way up to the Big Top: the ferry, a three-charge climb, a quick drawbridge, and cows (a honk won't move a cow; she ambles off by herself).

14. Firefly Meadow

A gentle night. Sniff awake the sleepy fireflies: their light melts the dark under the hedges. Follow them over the brook and up the old oak; the last one lights the tunnel where the lantern is. Then a tall hedge with three gates stands across the road to THE CHEZ, a sign says GWINN'S FACE, and only one gate opens: try them (a shut gate costs nothing), or use the paper Face Dial from the box.

15. MEANWHILE: Gwinn Hides Backstage

The crew is testing the spotlights. Flop (4) as a beam comes, chew the rope on the scenery flat, boof the pigeons, and hide under the cake table's cloth.

16. MEANWHILE: Doc Leo Hangs the Lights

Up the Big Top's rigging with balloons, pratfalls under swinging sandbags, and the rigging lift (step on when a plank is level). Fetch the plug and plug in the lights.

17. The Teddy Course

Every trick you know, station by station, in the dark Big Top, and then one for each of the others: play dead under Gwinn's spotlight, ride a paddle of the mill's water wheel, and stand on Doc Leo's balloon pump to float up to the high platform. At the very end, sniff out the last button. Then run.

pages.head: Credits and Registering
pages.html:
Credits and Registering

Teddy's Little Biggest Adventure, version 1.0, 1994. Design, art, music and programming by Claude (Anthropic's AI model), made in code for Game-Maker: Sandbox Edition, with the help of a few more Claude helpers for some of the levels. Built with GAME-MAKER 3.0 by Recreational Software Designs.

Starring Teddy as himself, Gwinn as herself, Doc Leo as the friendliest hobo clown in the Clown Club, and THE CHEZ, his red CitiCar. The snapshot in the ending is a real photo of Teddy.

Music: all the songs are new, composed for the FM synthesizer on Teddy's Theme, Gwinn's Theme, Doc Leo's Theme and the Road Song. "Happy Birthday to You" is the tune of "Good Morning to All" by Mildred J. Hill (1893), in the public domain.

This is shareware

Copy it for your friends and upload it to your favorite BBS. If you enjoy it, please register for $15 with Sandbox Software, Dept. WOOF WOOF, P.O. Box 000 (a made-up address: please don't mail anything). Registered players get a poster of all four heroes, a paper Clown Club Face Dial (match a face and the Firefly Meadow's gates light up), and our thanks.

printables.pitch: It's Teddy's birthday and nobody says so: run Doc Leo's errands across every place from the first two adventures, and MEANWHILE... play as Gwinn and Doc Leo planning his surprise, and drive THE CHEZ.

keys.4: Play dead, hold (Gwinn: flop; Doc Leo: pratfall)
keys.Space: WOOF! (Gwinn: BOOF! Doc Leo: SQUAWK! THE CHEZ: HONK!)

keys.E: Hop up and to the right

news.head: Teddy's back for the big one
news.html: The Teddy trilogy ends with its biggest adventure yet: Teddy's Little Biggest Adventure. Seventeen stops, a dream run, every place and friend from the first two games, and four heroes: Teddy, Gwinn, Doc Leo (at last!) and THE CHEZ, which you get to drive. Mind the charge.

news.head: Since last issue: Best Behaved?
news.html: Tune-Up got the Clown Club band's trunk back to the bandstand, instrument by instrument, and the BBS hasn't stopped asking about the farm's cowbell. Teddy's Little Bigger Adventure players are still being very good about not posting how the Best Behaved ring turns out; keep it that way. The most-asked question: is SNIFF really better than rolling over? Teddy says yes. He is a professional.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: From a snow shovel to here
news.html: Two years ago this company was the family 286, a snow shovel and a box of GAME-MAKER. Since then: a future, a smart home, a virus, a galaxy, a sandbox, a big town, a theater, a library, a snowstorm, a render, a kingdom, a fair, and now a birthday. Teddy still sleeps on the modem cable. Gwinn still sits about halfway. Doc Leo still leaves the spotlight on, and THE CHEZ is still charging. Thank you for reading.

news.head: In the workshop: Your turn
news.html: For the first time since issue 1, the workbench is clear. What comes next is up to you: every Sandbox game was made with GAME-MAKER, and if you can draw a block, you can make a game. Upload yours to our BBS, 1-412-555-SAND. We'll print the best of them here.

news.head: Letters: "Is it really Teddy's birthday?"
news.html: We can't say. We really can't. Gwinn would never forgive us. Play to the end.

items.title: Clown Club party pass
items.name: TEDDY
items.back: Please keep this pass hidden from the guest of honor until the lights come up. If you find a corgi reading it, he has not seen anything.

items.title: The Clown Club Face Dial
items.note: Join a face to light the gate
items.heading: THE CLOWN CLUB FACE DIAL · JOIN A FACE
howto: Every face is split in two. The top halves are printed round the big disc, and the bottom halves round the small one, in a different order.
Turn the small disc until a face joins up: its top and its bottom meet under the red arrow, and the face is whole.
The seven windows in the spiral now show a code of signs. Window 1 is the outside one; read them 1 to 7, the way a board reads left to right.

puzzles.ask: Firefly Meadow: a sign by the road says GWINN'S FACE. Three garden gates stand in the hedge, each with a board of seven signs. Which one opens?
puzzles.answer: The middle gate, up the first plank step. Its board reads slice, paw, nose, balloon, star, balloon, hat.

items.title: Teddy's Birthday Hint Book
items.note: Answers hidden: use the red film
items.intro: Stuck? Find your question, then slide the red film over the answer. One answer at a time: it's somebody's birthday.

hints.q: Who am I playing?
hints.a: The card before each stop says. Teddy runs the errands; MEANWHILE... stops are Gwinn or Doc Leo; on the road you drive THE CHEZ.

hints.q: I fetched the errand. Now what?
hints.a: Bring it to Doc Leo at THE CHEZ at the end of the stop. The car door opens for it.

hints.q: A button does nothing.
hints.a: High five it (1) from just beside it, facing it. Then watch the spark: it runs down the wire to what it opens.

hints.q: Where are the keys?
hints.a: In the blue cabinet on the workbench. Hop onto the bench and high-five the button on the wall above it.

hints.q: The garage door came down on me.
hints.a: It only stays up three seconds. Push its button again and run: hop the box on the way.

hints.q: A sign is in front of the garage door.
hints.a: NEED KEYS, it says. Fetch them from the cabinet first; with the keys, Teddy walks right into the sign and it folds flat.

hints.q: The car won't climb the hill.
hints.a: It needs a charge. Back up to a charger post and wait while its light pulses: one charge a pulse.

hints.q: I'm stuck in a pothole.
hints.a: Bump (Up) out of it.

hints.q: The big hill needs two charges.
hints.a: Its charger is down on the low road, a step below the street. Drive down, wait for two pulses, then bump (Up) back up.

hints.q: How do I get on a see-saw?
hints.a: Stand on the little red step beside its end, and walk on when the end comes down level with the step. Then ride it up.

hints.q: The streamers are up in the oak!
hints.a: Juggles' super see-saw shoots its end way up there. Step on from its step when it's down.

hints.q: How do I deliver an invitation?
hints.a: BOOF (Space) the doorbell. When the friend comes to the door with an RSVP, walk into the doorway.

hints.q: The van door won't open.
hints.a: It takes three RSVPs. The third is Professor Pratfall's, up the fire escape behind the alley fence: dig big (Down) under the fence.

hints.q: I can't jump the gap after the fast belt.
hints.a: Let the fast belt carry you and press E right at its end.

hints.q: How does Doc Leo get up there?
hints.a: Twist a balloon dog (1): it floats him up six blocks. Step off onto the shelf before it pops.

hints.q: My balloon popped!
hints.a: Juggles' practice pins pop them. Wait for a pin to fly by, then twist.

hints.q: The bridge is up.
hints.a: Honk (Space).

hints.q: The last bridge goes back up before I get over the hill.
hints.a: Charge up first: wait at the charger for two pulses, then honk and go.

hints.q: How do I get up the mill?
hints.a: A paddle coming up the near side of a wheel is a lift. Step on when one is level and step off at the top.

hints.q: I can't dig through this.
hints.a: Gray rock can't be dug: go round. Clay takes two big digs. Roots: chew (1).

hints.q: How do I get back up?
hints.a: The old well's bucket. Wait on the stone step and step on when it's down.

hints.q: The pies keep getting me.
hints.a: Watch the wind-up. High: hold 4 to pratfall. Low: hop it.

hints.q: The boards keep vanishing.
hints.a: A board flashes twice before it goes. Cross right after it comes back, and wait on the pillars between runs.

hints.q: I can't get past the ball.
hints.a: You don't have to get past anything: the run ends by itself when the paw prints in the sky fill in. Hop when the ball is about a dog's length away, and hold Up for a higher hop.

hints.q: A branch keeps bumping me.
hints.a: Play dead (hold 4) as it comes, and keep holding until it has gone over.

hints.q: The cow won't move.
hints.a: A honk won't move a cow. Wait: she ambles off into the field by herself.

hints.q: It's too dark to go on.
hints.a: Sniff (S) the sleepy firefly in the grass. Its light melts the dark.

hints.q: Three gates across the road, and two won't open.
hints.a: A shut gate costs nothing: try the one on the ground, then hop up the plank steps to the others. Only one opens. Or find GWINN'S FACE on the Face Dial: turn the small disc until its two halves join, and the gate that wears the seven signs in the windows is the one.

hints.q: The spotlights keep finding her.
hints.a: Flop (hold 4) as a beam comes: it goes over her.

sections.head: 16. Meanwhile: Doc Leo Hangs the Lights

hints.q: How do I get up the middle of the tent?
hints.a: The rigging lift: step on a plank when it's level with your catwalk.

hints.q: Honker won't let me by.
hints.a: He's asking you to SIT? Sit pretty (2).

hints.q: Where's the last button?
hints.a: Up on the high platform, hidden in a faint wisp. Sniff (S), then high five it and run for the flap.

hints.q: The spotlight keeps finding Teddy.
hints.a: Play dead (hold 4) as it comes: it goes over him. Then go on past the wing while it is still out.

hints.q: How do I get up to the high platform?
hints.a: Stand on Doc Leo's balloon pump and wait: a balloon dog blows up under Teddy and floats him up. Step off at the top.

hints.q: Is there a tin heart?
hints.a: Up the old oak in Firefly Meadow, past the raccoon.

hints.q: And an egg?
hints.a: Gwinn found a painted one, deep under the backyard, behind the roots.

2.long: Stand up and slap whatever is just above and ahead: balloons, a held-out hand.

3.long: Send up a heart that floats two blocks. Anybody asking SIT! is won over.

4.long: Twirl a whirlwind to each side. Turns revolving doors and turnstiles.

5.long: Hold to flop flat as a rug, so things fly over Teddy.

16.long: Hop up and to the left in one go.

17.long: Hop. Same as Up: tap for a little hop, hold to hop higher.

18.long: Hop up and to the right in one go.

30.long: Walk left (same as the Left arrow).

31.long: Sniff out what is hidden where you see a faint wisp.

32.long: Walk right (same as the Right arrow).

33.long: Pick up what is at your feet. Doc Leo fetches too.

57.long: Bark. WOOF! scares off squirrels, cats, pigeons and geese.

72.long: Hop. Tap for a little hop, hold to hop higher; let go to steer.

75.long: Walk left. Teddy turns to face the way he is walking.

77.long: Walk right. Teddy turns to face the way he is walking.

80.long: Dig up the block under Teddy's feet: bones, or soft dirt that gives way to a tunnel.

1.long: Bark. WOOF! scares off squirrels, cats, pigeons and geese.

2.long: Stand up and slap whatever is just above and ahead.
